subsystems.name: Mirror swarm
subsystems.role: a Dyson swarm of lightweight reflectors that redirects a star's own light onto one small target zone.

subsystems.name: Ablation target zone
subsystems.role: a patch of stellar surface heated until material streams outward as plasma — the engine's exhaust.

subsystems.name: Collimating nozzle
subsystems.role: shapes the escaping plasma into a directed jet rather than a spherical blow-off.

subsystems.name: Fusion second stage
subsystems.role: adds thrust and enables steering by fusing captured hydrogen with boron.

subsystems.name: Fuel and mass handling
subsystems.role: captures plasma from the jet, separates hydrogen and helium, and imports the boron that the star cannot supply.

subsystems.name: Attitude control
subsystems.role: keeps the jet aligned and points the counter-thrust so the star travels on a chosen course.

buildSteps.title: Build the swarm
buildSteps.detail: An industrial base enormous enough to dismantle asteroids and planets and turn them into trillions of thin mirror elements would have to exist first — a precondition, not a build step in itself.

buildSteps.title: Phase the mirrors
buildSteps.detail: The reflectors are placed in orbits that let them all aim at one spot. Collectively they concentrate the star's entire output onto a region about a hundred kilometres across.

buildSteps.title: Heat the target zone
buildSteps.detail: At the focus the surface temperature climbs until stellar material ablates away — the star begins to blow off a plasma stream under its own focused light.

buildSteps.title: Shroud the flow in magnets
buildSteps.detail: A magnetic nozzle surrounds the ablation zone. Plasma follows the field lines and is squeezed into a collimated jet, which pushes the star the opposite way.

buildSteps.title: Install the fusion stage
buildSteps.detail: A structure sits in or beside the jet and collects hydrogen and helium from it. Boron — the only fuel the star cannot provide — is brought in from elsewhere.

buildSteps.title: Drive the accelerator
buildSteps.detail: Protons are accelerated into boron at energies high enough for fusion, chosen because it yields charged particles rather than damaging neutrons.

buildSteps.title: Vector the thrust
buildSteps.detail: The fusion products are expelled through magnetic coils, giving a steerable counter-jet. By balancing the main jet and the counter-thrust, the star is driven on a course rather than merely drifting.

buildSteps.title: Cruise and correct
buildSteps.detail: Over very long spans the aim is adjusted to keep the star and its worlds on a chosen trajectory.

prerequisites.why: without the mirrors there is no way to concentrate a star's output onto one point.
it supplies the steerable second-stage thrust; it is far harder to ignite than deuterium–tritium and has never been achieved.
existing plasma thrusters show the principle at metres, not at the millions of kilometres needed to shape a stellar jet.
predicting how a star responds to concentrated ablation is required before any of it could be attempted.
the boron and the swarm itself have to come from material and production outside Earth.

pathway.milestone: the concept exists only as published theoretical work: Matthew Caplan's 2019 paper in Acta Astronautica on stellar engines
pathway.unlocks: a quantitative target for how a star could be steered, and a clear list of what is missing.

pathway.milestone: a partial or complete Dyson swarm used first for power, not propulsion
pathway.unlocks: the mirror infrastructure the engine depends on, built for its own sake.

pathway.milestone: controlled ablation and magnetic collimation demonstrated on a small or low-mass star
pathway.unlocks: proof that a star's own material can be turned into a jet.

pathway.milestone: a working boron-fusion second stage in space
pathway.unlocks: steering, not just drifting — the star becomes a vehicle.
moving a whole planetary system away from a dying star or towards another one.
